newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady - up $1 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady - up $1 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher amid light hog marketings as producers concentrate on harvesting, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were expected to range from $60.00 to $61.00. Illinois top hog prices at the plant also could range from $60.00 to $61.00.
Indiana and Ohio top hog prices were seen at $59.00 at plants, the dealers said.

Lighter hog marketings were reflected in USDA hog slaughter estimates, with Thursday pegged at 368,000 head, compared with 374,000 a week ago. Week-to-date was estimated at 1.442 million head, down 1.1 percent from a week ago.

Cash hog price strength Friday could be offset by concern that pork prices were heading lower and by talk that several major packers could resist higher hog prices by cutting back slaughter operations early next week, the dealers said.
"Their (packers') margins are slipping because they're paying out the money and not getting a return on the product," said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
